answer.sourceLine: Genuinely his, and from his first book. Wikiquote’s sourced section for Unlimited Power prints the sentence and cites page 198. One caveat worth having: that page number belongs to a later printing rather than the 1986 first edition — the same Wikiquote section cites a page 413, which will not fit the 1986 printing the Internet Archive catalogues at 376 pages, and the section links a 2003 edition of the book.

source.excerpt: The quality of your life is the quality of your communication.
trail: Wikiquote’s sourced section ↗ for Unlimited Power prints this sentence and cites page 198. We read the page’s raw wikitext rather than a summary, so the wording is as Wikiquote states it.

The book is independently confirmed: Wikipedia ↗ gives Unlimited Power as Robbins’s first book, published by Simon & Schuster on 15 June 1986, and the Internet Archive catalogue record ↗ gives “New York : Simon and Schuster, 1986,” 376 pages.

Why this page hedges the page number rather than the quote: the same Wikiquote section also cites a page 413, which cannot be a 376-page printing, and the section’s header links a later edition of the book. We checked that linked volume — Google Books ↗ confirms it as Unlimited Power: The New Science Of Personal Achievement by Tony Robbins, Simon and Schuster, and presents it as a 2008 printing (Wikiquote’s own link text calls it the 2003 edition). Either way it is not the 1986 first edition, so 198 is a real citation to a later printing.

Limit of what we checked: we did not read the book. The Internet Archive copy is lending-restricted and Google Books returned a bot challenge, so page 198 was not confirmed against the book’s own text.

author.bio: Born Anthony J. Mahavorić in North Hollywood, California, Robbins has worked as a speaker and coach since the late 1970s. Unlimited Power (1986) was his first book and the foundation of the seminar business that followed; Awaken the Giant Within (1991) was the second. Between them they are the source of most of the sentences quoted under his name.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Unlimited Power was Robbins’s first book and the one that built his audience, and this sentence is its argument in miniature: that how you talk — to others and to yourself — is not a surface skill but the thing that sets the ceiling on everything else.
It is also the most quotable line in a book full of them, which is why it turns up on slides far more often than the chapter it came from.
detailsBody: The attribution here is not in any doubt; the citation is. Quote collections reproduce “p. 198” from Wikiquote without noting that the figure tracks a later printing, and a reader who opens a 1986 hardcover at page 198 may well not find it. That is a small thing, but it is exactly the sort of small thing a citation is supposed to get right.
